schema.label: Design
schema.text: Open-label phase I/II trial of neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, then nelfinavir and stereotactic body radiotherapy, for non-metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The trial closed early when the chemotherapy backbone was no longer standard.

schema.label: Sequence
schema.text: Three 3-week cycles of gemcitabine, leucovorin, fluorouracil, and oregovomab. Milligram doses of the cytotoxic drugs were not in the sections read. Nelfinavir 1250 mg twice daily for 5 weeks, with 40 Gy in 5 fractions during the third week. Another chemoimmunotherapy cycle follows, then pancreaticoduodenectomy if resectable, then three more cycles, for 7 cycles total. If CA-125 is at least 10 units/mL, oregovomab 2 mg is given for 7 doses: 3 before radiotherapy, 1 between radiotherapy and resection, and 3 after surgery. Patients below that CA-125 level do not receive oregovomab.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: 40 Gy in 5 daily fractions. At least 95 percent of the PTV is covered, or 93 percent if bowel constraints cannot be met. Maximum PTV dose does not exceed 110 percent. Stomach and small bowel maximum point dose is 32 Gy. Other constraints are cited from a prior study and are not restated here.

brief.schema_source: Lin et al., American journal of clinical oncology 2019 (PMID 31513018). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 19 or older. Newly diagnosed, pathologically confirmed, non-metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma no larger than 10 cm, including resectable, borderline, and unresectable disease. Karnofsky performance status at least 60 percent and laboratories appropriate for chemotherapy. Numeric cutoffs were not in the sections read.
Biliary or gastroduodenal obstruction is allowed if drained or bypassed first. A prior malignancy is allowed if treatment finished more than 5 years earlier and there is no clinical evidence of it.

Excluded: prior radiotherapy overlapping the 20 percent isodose, contraindication to staging laparoscopy, allergy to murine protein or a protocol drug, uncontrolled intercurrent illness, autoimmune or immunodeficiency disease, inability to consent, pregnancy or nursing, contraindicated concomitant medicines, other investigational agents, and hepatic insufficiency.

pretreatment.note: Blood counts, chemistries, CA-125, and CA 19-9. Contrast CT, MRI, PET, and/or endoscopic or laparoscopic ultrasound.
Confirms no peritoneal metastases. Two fiducials are placed about 2 cm apart.

during.note: Medical and radiation oncology. Toxicity uses CTCAE version 3.0.

followup.window: Every 3 months in year 1, every 4 months in year 2, then twice a year
followup.note: Contrast CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and CA 19-9. Response uses RECIST 1.1.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution phase 3 trial comparing radiosurgery platforms for 1 to 4 brain metastases. Primary endpoint is cumulative incidence of symptomatic radionecrosis, CTCAE version 3.0 grades 2 to 4. The design expected about 10 percent at one year on the gamma-ray arm and about 1 percent on the linac arm, and required 250 patients.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Age (65 or younger versus older than 65), extracranial metastases, and number of metastases (one versus two to four).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 1:1 permuted blocks.

arms.label: Gamma Knife Perfexion
arms.text: Frame and volumetric MRI. Target is the enhancing tumor with no margin and no image guidance. 24 Gy for metastases 20 mm or smaller and 20 Gy for 21 to 30 mm, prescribed to the 50 percent isodose so that the 50 percent line covers the target.

arms.label: Edge linac
arms.text: Open-face mask. GTV is the enhancing tumor. PTV is a 2 mm isotropic margin. 24 Gy to the mean PTV dose for diameter 20 mm or smaller, and 20 Gy for 21 to 30 mm. Planning objective is PTV V95 percent above 95 percent, and more than 98 percent of the GTV covered by 98 percent of the prescribed dose.

brief.schema_source: Scorsetti et al., Radiation Oncology (London, England) 2023 (PMID 36750848). The full text was read.
eligibility: Age 18 to 85, Karnofsky performance status at least 70, histologically confirmed solid tumor, 1 to 4 brain metastases up to 30 mm, RPA class 1 or 2, and estimated survival at least 3 months by disease-specific GPA.
Active extracranial disease and systemic therapy are allowed.
Excluded: small-cell lung cancer, hematologic malignancy, pregnancy, prior whole-brain radiotherapy, and bevacizumab for at least two months after radiosurgery.

publications.title: Intensity-modulated radiation therapy and doxorubicin in thyroid cancer: A prospective phase 2 trial.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-institution nonrandomized phase 2 trial of intensity-modulated radiotherapy with or without concurrent doxorubicin for gross residual or unresectable non-anaplastic differentiated thyroid cancer. Primary endpoint is 2-year locoregional progression-free survival.

schema.label: Radiotherapy
schema.text: Supine, five-point mask. GTV is gross disease on CT, PET, and/or MRI and examination. CTV includes the GTV, thyroid bed, tracheoesophageal groove, and level VI and upper mediastinal nodes. PTV expands GTV and CTV by 3 to 5 mm. Planned doses are 70 Gy in 33 to 35 fractions to gross disease, 66 Gy in 33 fractions to close or positive margins, 60 Gy in 30 to 33 fractions to the operative or tumor bed, and 54 Gy in 30 fractions to low-risk central neck nodes. The lateral neck is not routine unless gross disease is present.

schema.label: Doxorubicin
schema.text: The first 8 patients received radiotherapy alone. From July 2014, weekly doxorubicin 10 mg/m2 was required during radiotherapy.

schema.label: Constraints
schema.text: Larynx maximum point dose under 70 Gy and mean under 45 Gy. Esophagus mean under 34 Gy. Lung mean under 21 Gy and V20 under 37 percent. Brachial plexus maximum under 65 Gy. Brainstem, optic nerves, and chiasm maximum under 54 Gy. Cord maximum under 45 Gy. Oral cavity mean under 40 Gy. Parotid mean under 26 Gy.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multi-institutional phase II trial of total neoadjuvant therapy and selective nonoperative management for MRI-staged stage II or III rectal adenocarcinoma amenable to total mesorectal excision. Both arms receive 5-FU or capecitabine-based chemoradiation. After neoadjuvant therapy, patients are restaged. Residual tumor at the primary site is treated with total mesorectal excision, and a clinical complete response is managed nonoperatively. The trial compares 3-year disease-free survival.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed rectal adenocarcinoma, MRI stage II (T3N0) or III (T1-3, N1-3), potentially resectable and amenable to total mesorectal excision.
No distant metastases. No prior pelvic radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or surgery for rectal cancer.
Age older than 18. Karnofsky above 60 percent or ECOG 0-2. No infection that needs systemic antibiotics.

ANC above 1.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin above 8.0 g/dL, platelets above 150,000/mm3, total bilirubin at most 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, and ALT at most 3 times the upper limit of normal. The published table's AST inequality is garbled, so it is not restated here.

Excluded: recurrent or unresectable primary tumor fixed to adjacent structures, creatinine above 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, prior pelvic radiotherapy, arterial thrombosis within 6 months, another malignancy within 5 years except treated skin cancer or in situ cervical cancer, and concurrent anticancer or experimental therapy.

Flexible sigmoidoscopy with a photograph and biopsy, proctoscopy, endorectal ultrasound, and pelvic MRI.
CT of the chest and abdomen. Pathology confirmation at the participating site before treatment.
